subject: Recap & next steps: FinServe discovery — feature-level costing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@finserve.io>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: FinServe discovery — feature-level costing

Emma / Amit — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. I captured the items you asked us to cost and the initial assumptions we agreed on: 

Summary of ask
- Pilot scope: 3 months, goal to validate Summarization + Compliance-check features across 2 product teams.
- Expected steady-state volume (post-pilot): ~50M tokens/month. Q1 2027 peak planning scenario: up to ~200M tokens/month.
- Initial budget range (guideline from FinServe): "$20k–$30k per month" for early production.

Redwood preliminary unit-econ framing (high-level)
- Price target you called out: <= $600 / 1M tokens (FinServe target).
- Example per-request math at $750 / 1M tokens (for reference): token unit cost = $0.00075 / token.
  - Summarization (avg 1.2k tokens req): ~1200 * $0.00075 = $0.90 / request.
  - Compliance-check (avg 300 tokens): ~300 * $0.00075 = $0.225 / request.
- With optimization (quantization + batching + cache) we expect a path to reduce inference cost by ~2.5–3x depending on latency SLOs and model choice.

Business KPIs you asked about
- Target gross margin on product features: 55–65% (you mentioned finance prefers >60%).
- CAC payback: FinServe target ~6–12 months; you indicated a preference toward faster payback if unit cost is higher.

Immediate next steps (owner / timing)
1) Redwood to share a feature-level cost workbook with three pricing scenarios (conservative, expected, optimized) — ATTACHED: FS-forecast-1Mtokens_breakdown.xlsx — ETA: EOD today (Karthik).
2) You to confirm committed pilot monthly volume (we proposed 20M/mo for pilot) and legal contact for an MAA/draft (Amit or procurement) — ETA: EOD Wed (FinServe).
3) Schedule 45-min follow-up to walk the workbook and pilot terms — suggested Wed 11/24 or Thu 11/25 (Karthik / Emma).

Notes on pilot commercial framing (quick)
- 3-month pilot: committed 20M tokens/mo with tiered consumption pricing. Example pilot price placeholders: Month1 $700 / 1M, Months2–3 $550 / 1M. Setup fee to cover integration & logging (~one-time).
- Post-pilot: committed production pricing to be negotiated; we can bake in a ramp schedule tied to committed volumes and performance SLAs.

If helpful, I can include a brief sensitivity table showing feature-level $/request at the three pricing scenarios — I included a small excerpt in the attached workbook.

Thanks — I’ll send the workbook now and follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

—
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: FS-MAA-draft-terms.pdf (pdf) --

From: Emma Rogers <emma.rogers@finserve.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@finserve.io>
Cc: FinServe Procurement <procurement@finserve.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinServe discovery — feature-level costing

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications before you finalize the workbook: 

1) Budget / pricing constraints: we can stretch to $25k/month for early production, but the program finance needs a path to <= $600 / 1M tokens at scale. If your optimized scenario is realistic, we can make a longer-term commitment.
2) Pilot volumes: 20M/mo for pilot sounds reasonable. We will try to commit if pilot performance matches SLAs.
3) Pilot requirements: private deployment (VPC) is preferred for Compliance team; is that supported for pilot or do you require hosted initially?
4) Legal: loop in procurement@finserve.io for the MAA; Amit will be our internal commercial lead.

Also please include a table showing per-feature $/request at both $750 and $550 / 1M token assumptions so finance can compare. Can you also note expected ops uplift (engineering support hours) for the pilot?

Available for a walkthrough Wed 11/24 10am–12pm PT.

—
Emma Rogers
Head of Product, FinServe
emma.rogers@finserve.io | +1 (617) 555-0291

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinServe discovery — feature-level costing

Emma — thanks for the quick clarification. Attached is the workbook with three scenarios and the per-feature sensitivity table you requested. I pasted the short excerpt below for convenience.

Excerpt: per-feature $/request at two price points
- Summarization (avg 1.2k tokens): 
  - $750 / 1M => $0.90 / request
  - $550 / 1M => $0.66 / request
- Compliance-check (avg 300 tokens): 
  - $750 / 1M => $0.225 / request
  - $550 / 1M => $0.165 / request

Pilot proposal (concrete)
- 3-month engagement; committed 20M tokens/mo; bucketed pricing: Month1 $700 / 1M, Months2–3 $550 / 1M.
- One-time integration & security review fee: $12,500 (covers VPC onboarding, audit logs, runbook).
- Ops support: dedicated Solutions Engineer 0.2 FTE during onboarding, then on-call support (SLAs to be defined).

Action items for FinServe
- Confirm pilot monthly commit (20M) and approval to share a sample of anonymized request traces for our cost modeling (we only need token distributions, not PII).
- Provide legal contact for the MAA (we’ll send a draft).

I’ll push a calendar invite for Wed 11/24 10am PT per your availability. If procurement needs a different time, let me know.

—
Karthik

Date: 2026-11-20T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap & next steps: FinServe discovery — feature-level costing

Internal — forwarding the FinServe thread and workbook. Quick internal notes / asks: 

- Margin check: proposed pilot pricing (~$700 then $550 / 1M) maps to an expected inference cost on our side of ~$260–$320 / 1M (depends on model choice & quant). That yields gross margins in the ~55–65% band for feature revenue assumptions but leaves limited headroom for aggressive discounts.
- CAC/payback: procurement signaled a ~$25k/mo budget target; if pilot converts at 50M/mo post-ramp we hit payback ~9 months with current ACV assumptions. If they only reach 30M/mo, payback extends >12 months.

Asks:
1) Marissa — do we have flexibility to approve the pilot commercial (one-time $12.5k setup + tiered pricing) or should I get a pricing exception?
2) Priyom — can you review the sensitivity sheet and flag any other cost levers (model variant, quantization, routing) we should call out in the customer walkthrough?

I’ll wait for your greenlight before I lock the pilot MAA and pricing in HubSpot.

—
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
